Re-downloaded the publisher PDF. You need the Ovid cookie set by first loading the /fulltext/ page; a cold request is 307-redirected to HTML. The PDF's md5 matches the researcher's file. I read all 6 pages at 150-300 dpi and every number checks:
- n: 156 recruited, 134 evaluable, +23 from the testosterone trial (5 former users, 18 non-users). Totals 157 = 83 users + 74 non-users.
- Table 1: users 1.79±0.075 m, 91.69±11.8 kg, 12.8±4.8% fat, FFMI 24.8±2.2. Non-users 1.80±0.074 m, 82.06±13.0 kg, 12.5±5.5% fat, FFMI 21.8±1.8.
- 'slope of 6.1 kg/m3' and 'Normalized FFMI = FFMI + 6.1 x (1.8 - h)', with 1.8 m as 'the mean height of the nonusers'. 6.3 appears only in the abstract.
- 37 (45%) users beyond the top non-user. 'all 74 nonusers produced urine samples negative'. Six non-users (8.1%) above 20% fat. Skinfold SE 3.4%, with the 25.0 vs 24.2 example. The 1.59 m (23.5) and 1.93 m (25.4) men, and the 'appeared more muscular' quote. The '67%' slip (52/83 is 63%).
Two nits:
- Table 1 says only 'FFMI'. 'Before height normalisation' is an inference; it makes almost no difference at these mean heights.
- 18 of the 74 non-users came from a testosterone trial in 'normal men', not from gyms, so 'drug-free lifters' (used in the recommendations) overstates the group.
checks.corrected: Note: 74 non-users = 56 gym-recruited athletes + 18 men from a testosterone trial. Table 1 FFMI normalisation not stated (inference).

I recounted Fig. 2 from my own 300-dpi render, with an independent column-projection script and by eye.
- Non-users, bins 17 to 24: 1, 5, 4, 16, 16, 13, 10, 9 (total 74).

Table 2 is transcribed exactly. Recomputed: mean 25.45, SD 1.549, max 28.0 (Delinger), min 22.6, 3 above 27, 13 above 25, 8 at or above 26. Slope 0.0418/yr (t = 0.75, so p ≈ 0.46 against the printed 0.44). Subsets: through 1944, 24.93 (max 27.3); through 1953, 25.57 (max 28.0). The Fig. 3 vs Table 2 bin discrepancy is confirmed. Method quotes confirmed: blind photo estimates, Park 1952 and Schaefer 1956 not rated, 'Todd T, personal communication', Willoughby 1970 as ref 21.
Caveat on the S conversion (S mean 25.8, max 29.2). It uses Todd's heights and weights, which are not Kouri's inputs. With Todd's H/W, Kouri's Grimek 1941 value (26.9) implies 21% fat, beyond Pope's recalled 16% maximum. So Kouri's Willoughby weights differ, at least for Grimek. The S figures are a rough estimate only. They are insensitive to height (±2 cm moves S about 0.2), so the conclusion holds.
Also, Helms notes possible testosterone access on the US West Coast from 1945 (uncorroborated), as well as Ziegler injecting Park and Grimek in 1954.
checks.corrected: Add: S conversion uses Todd's heights, not Kouri's (Willoughby) inputs; at least Grimek 1941's inputs differ (Todd's H/W would imply ~21% fat in Kouri's value).

checks.issue:
Formula and constants confirmed on weighttraining.nz (22.667, 17.01; metric 322.4, 241.9, which I re-derived exactly) and fitmatic (22.6670, 17.0104; 'approximately 300 natural bodybuilding champions spanning from 1947 to 2010'). McDonald's text confirms '7″ wrist and 8.75″ ankle'. His table gives 189/198/206 lb and LBM 170/178/185; I recompute 170.24, 177.80, 185.48. All men: 25.29 and 25.84 (P5 24.30, P95 26.97). S medians 29.71 (155-160 cm, n = 34) and 23.82 (190-195 cm). Nuances:
(a) All three McDonald checks use one wrist/ankle pair and one fat level. They confirm the H^1.5 term and the overall scale, not the wrist and ankle constants separately or the F/224 term. The two calculators agreeing covers that.
(b) Secondary accounts of the data disagree. Fitmatic says ~300 champions, 1947-2010. bonytobeastly says 'hundreds of natural bodybuilders, strength athletes, and regular gym goers' with data 'from the 1950s and 60s', which reaches into the steroid era.
(c) Fitmatic attributes the ±3% caveat to Butt, without a citation; it is not unattributed.
(d) The McDonald URL now redirects to /muscle-gain/genetic-muscular-potential.
checks.corrected: Add to notes: secondary sample descriptions conflict (fitmatic ~300 champions 1947-2010 vs bonytobeastly 'hundreds' incl. gym-goers, 1950s-60s data); the McDonald checks validate H^1.5 and overall scale at one frame only.

checks.issue:
The numbers are right: inclusion criterion 3 quoted correctly; 339 men by DXA, mean 19.78 (19.56-20.00); rugby n = 39, 21.33. Table S7 male 95th percentiles: rugby 25.79 (23.54-28.71), wrestling/judo 24.60, handball 23.64, soccer 23.47, volleyball 23.31. Missing caveats that change how much the anchor weighs:
(1) Table 1 shows the rugby DXA subsample was aged 16-28, mean 18.2 ± 2.1 years. These are mostly juniors and still maturing, so this percentile says little about an adult natural ceiling.
(2) The 182.8 cm rugby height comes from the separate n = 62 height/weight sample, not the n = 39 DXA group.
(3) The percentiles are parametric empirical-Bayes estimates (a normal model that borrows across sports), not observed values.
(4) The paper does not say who tested or when; 'negative test outcomes for performance-enhancing drugs' is only an inclusion criterion.
checks.corrected: Add to label/notes: 'rugby DXA group n=39, age 16-28 (mean 18.2); model-smoothed percentiles; height 182.8 cm is from the n=62 anthropometry sample; testing not described beyond the inclusion criterion'. Treat as weak for an adult natural limit.

missing:
1. S-axis sample maximum. The chart ranks by S, and on S Kouri's highest drug-free non-user is the 1.59 m man at about 26.6 (Fig. 1 plus the text), not 25. The recommendation plots 25 as a solid 'sample maximum' tick. That is right only for a 1.80 m man, so it must carry the label 'height-normalised FFMI', or the S tick must sit at 26.6 and be described as one short man.
2. Santos 2014 age. The rugby DXA subsample is 16–28 years old, mean 18.2. That should come with the anchor. As it stands, it is presented as the one drug-tested upper tail.
3. Todd's Grimek weight. Her 32.0 (S 32.5) depends on a 221-lb weight in 1941 that conflicts with the 195 lb in the 1956 Mr America program already in builds.json. Her own Pearl caption also contradicts her table.
4. Method differences. Kouri used skinfolds (SE 3.4% fat, about ±0.8–1 FFMI unit by the paper's own example). Trexler, Currier and Santos used DXA (lean mass plus bone mineral). Kondo, Hattori and Abe used hydrodensitometry. The band puts all of these side by side with only a body-fat caveat; it needs a 'methods differ by about ±1 unit' note.
5. Who the non-users were. 18 of Kouri's 74 non-users came from a testosterone trial in 'normal men', not from gyms. Todd also criticises the sample as not elite (non-user mean FFMI 21.8). The '74 drug-free lifters' label should reflect both.
6. Currier drug testing. It is unknown, not 'none'. The recommendation's 'these studies did no testing' is supported only for Trexler.
7. Kondo's wording. Kondo's S of 33.9 is above the mean of about 31.5 for Kouri's enhanced magazine bodybuilders, so 'just below the enhanced pros' can mislead. Say it falls inside the enhanced bodybuilders' range, and that its FFM includes organ and water mass at 33% fat.
8. Unresearched leads (not verified here; check before use): DXA or BodPod data on drug-tested natural bodybuilders beyond Chappell and Rossow, e.g. contest-prep studies of natural male bodybuilders (Mitchell et al. 2018, Eur J Sport Sci) and case studies (Kistler 2014, Pardue 2017, IJSNEM). Also WADA/IPF-tested weightlifters or powerlifters with DXA. Todd 2008 (pp. 17–20) also gives an estimated mean FFMI of 29.06 for nine pre-1958 strongmen (Sandow and others). It is very low quality but the highest 'pre-steroid' claim in the same source, so it is worth a note if the Todd bracket is shown.
9. Helms on pre-steroid status. Helms says West Coast bodybuilders could possibly have obtained testosterone from 1945, though this is uncorroborated. That weakens the pre-steroid status of the 1945+ winners a little, not only the 1955–59 entries.
10. Overlapping samples. The Kondo, Hattori and Abe sumo papers share authors and probably share subjects, so they are not independent confirmations.
verdict:
The research holds up, with a few corrections.

The central claims hold:
- I fetched the Kouri 1995 PDF from Ovid myself; it is the same file as the researcher's. Every quoted sentence and table value matches. The 6.1 slope in the methods (6.3 only in the abstract), the blind photo-based Mr America fat estimates, and the non-users' 12.5±5.5% fat are all confirmed. My own script reproduces the Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 counts exactly.
- The Todd, Trexler, Currier, Santos, Kondo, Hattori, Abe, Berkhan, McDonald, Aragon and Butt-repost sources all say what the notes quote.
- The derived numbers recompute: the Kouri and Todd statistics, the Butt formula against McDonald's table, the ANSUR II frame medians and predicted FFMI/S, the Berkhan and Kondo conversions, and the S conversions.

Corrections needed:
(1) Todd 2008. The cited pages are wrong: the article is pp. 3–22, with the Mr America analysis on pp. 14–16. Her top value of 32.0 rests on a 221-lb Grimek weight that conflicts with the 195 lb in builds.json's 1956 contest program. At 195 lb it would be about 27.9.
(2) Santos 2014. The rugby DXA group was aged 16–28, mean 18.2. Its percentiles are model-smoothed, not observed. It is a weak anchor for an adult natural limit.
(3) On the chart's S axis, Kouri's highest non-user is about 26.6 (the 1.59 m man), not 25. The recommended '25 sample maximum' tick needs a 'normalised FFMI, equals S only at 1.80 m' label.
(4) Smaller nits: the Berkhan data-point range (22.7–23.6, not 23.0–23.5), Aragon's '2–3 years', the Currier S upper end (28.0, not 28.1), Moreno's 2 men + 6 women, and the unverified 'non-refereed' claim about Iron Game History.

The recommendations are sound in structure: a soft band, anchors typed by kind, no 'ceiling' wording, and rate models kept off the chart. They overstate the evidence in three places:
- '74 drug-free lifters': 18 of the 74 came from a testosterone trial in ordinary men.
- 'These studies did no testing': supported for Trexler only; unknown for Currier.
- 'Just below the enhanced pros' for the sumo wrestler: his S of 33.9 is inside the enhanced bodybuilders' range.

The band also needs a methods caveat: skinfolds, DXA and densitometry can differ by about 1 FFMI unit.

The builds.json correction list is accurate and should be applied. The file is shared, so it needs a STATUS.md claim first.
